## DEEP AUDIT: RANKORA CAREER PAGE SYSTEM

### 1. CURRENT FEATURES

**What the Career Page Shows:**
- Branded header with company logo and name
- Sticky header with navigation
- Hero section with:
  - Large company name display
  - Optional tagline
  - Optional about/company description (plaintext only, max 2000 chars)
  - Badge showing total open positions count
- Search functionality across job titles, departments, and locations
- Multi-filter system:
  - Department filter (dynamic from job data, appears only if >1 department)
  - Location filter (dynamic from job data, appears only if >1 location)
- Job listing cards displaying:
  - Job title
  - Location, Department, Employment Type, Salary Range (with icons)
  - "Posted X days ago" timestamp
  - Social sharing buttons (LinkedIn, X/Twitter, copy link)
  - "Apply Now" button (styled with brand color)
- Empty state messaging when no positions match filters
- Footer with Rankora attribution and legal disclaimer

**What Settings Are Configurable:**
- Company name
- URL slug (auto-generated from company name, with availability checking)
- Logo URL (external image link)
- Brand color (6-digit hex only, no shortcuts like #fff)
- Tagline (max 160 chars)
- About/company description (max 2000 chars, plaintext)
- Is Active toggle (controls public visibility)
- Per-job publishing toggle (which jobs appear on career page)
- Career page URL preview (copy and open links)

---

### 2. DATABASE SCHEMA

**career_page_config Table:**
```
- id (UUID, PK)
- team_id (UUID, UNIQUE, FK to teams table, CASCADE delete)
- slug (TEXT, UNIQUE, validated: ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9\-]{1,58}[a-z0-9]$)
- company_name (TEXT, NOT NULL)
- logo_url (TEXT, nullable)
- brand_color (TEXT, DEFAULT '#6366f1', validated: ^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$)
- tagline (TEXT, nullable, max 160 chars)
- about (TEXT, nullable, max 2000 chars)
- is_active (BOOLEAN, DEFAULT false)
- created_at, updated_at (TIMESTAMPTZ)
```

**Jobs Table Extensions:**
```
Added 5 new columns to jobs table:
- location (TEXT, nullable)
- department (TEXT, nullable)
- employment_type (TEXT, DEFAULT 'Full-time')
- salary_range (TEXT, nullable)
- is_published (BOOLEAN, DEFAULT false)
```

**Job Fields Available:**
The public career page shows: title, location, department, employment_type, salary_range, created_at

The admin JobMetadataSection in JobDetailView allows editing:
- Location (freetext, e.g. "San Francisco, CA")
- Department (freetext, e.g. "Engineering")
- Employment Type (SELECT: Full-time, Part-time, Contract, Internship, Freelance)
- Salary Range (freetext, e.g. "$80k - $120k")

**Existing Job Fields (from broader system):**
- id, user_id, team_id, title, job_description, status, is_published
- must_weight, nice_weight, optional_weight (for ranking)
- jd_analysis_json, dynamic_weights_json, jd_embedding (for AI)
- processing_started_at, completed_at (lifecycle)

---

### 3. JOB METADATA FIELDS

Currently available job metadata fields on the public page:

| Field | Type | Source | Visibility |
|-------|------|--------|------------|
| title | string | jobs.title | Public |
| location | string | jobs.location | Public |
| department | string | jobs.department | Public |
| employment_type | string | jobs.employment_type | Public |
| salary_range | string | jobs.salary_range | Public |
| created_at | timestamp | jobs.created_at | Public (formatted as "Posted X days ago") |

All are **optional** fields (nullable in database except employment_type which defaults to "Full-time").

---

### 4. MISSING PRODUCTION FEATURES

#### **SEO & Meta Tags**
- No `<head>` meta tags per page (og:title, og:description, og:image, etc.)
- No canonical URLs set
- No structured schema markup (JSON-LD for JobPosting)
- No meta description per job or per page
- Page title is static: `Careers at {company_name} | Rankora` (no per-job titles)
- No robots.txt or sitemap generation

#### **Custom Branding & Styling**
- Only logo URL and one brand color supported (very limited)
- No custom CSS injection capability
- No font family customization
- No custom footer/header HTML
- No custom domain support (locked to /careers/:slug on Rankora domain)
- No dark mode toggle (uses system theme only)
- No page-wide styling options (padding, border radius, spacing)

#### **Job Listing Filtering & Discovery**
- No job categories beyond department/location
- No job type tags beyond the hardcoded employment_type field
- No skill-based filtering
- No experience level filtering
- No salary filtering/ranges
- No date range filtering for posted jobs

#### **Search & Navigation**
- Search is basic substring matching only
- No search analytics (what candidates search for)
- No featured/promoted jobs
- No job recommendations
- No breadcrumb navigation
- No related jobs suggestions

#### **Social & Sharing**
- Social buttons present but minimal (LinkedIn, X, copy link only)
- No Facebook/email sharing
- No Pinterest
- No hashtag suggestions
- No pre-filled share text optimization

#### **Analytics & Tracking**
- No view tracking per job
- No application count tracking
- No click-through tracking
- No Google Analytics integration
- No conversion tracking
- No A/B testing capability
- No traffic source attribution
- No bounce rate/time-on-page metrics

#### **Application Tracking**
- No views counter on job listings
- No application counter
- No "hot job" indicators (popular jobs)
- No weekly/monthly application trends
- No per-candidate source tracking (where they came from)

#### **Rich Content**
- Job descriptions are plaintext only in job_description field
- No markdown support
- No HTML formatting
- No embedded videos
- No image galleries
- No benefits/perks display fields
- No team member profiles linked to jobs

#### **Job Lifecycle Management**
- No job expiry dates/auto-closure
- No job status indicators (new, closing soon, filled)
- No "applications closing soon" warnings
- No job renewal/refresh timestamps
- No archived jobs view
- No draft jobs (only publish/unpublish toggle)
- No scheduling jobs for future publication

#### **Email & Notifications**
- No email alerts for new jobs
- No job subscription/watchlist
- No email to candidate when you apply
- No "new matching jobs" alerts
- No weekly job digest
- No SMS notifications

#### **Advanced Configuration**
- No multi-language support (slug language varies, content doesn't)
- No timezone considerations
- No custom email domain for reply-to
- No GDPR/compliance fields (privacy policy acceptance, etc.)
- No integration with ATS systems
- No Zapier/webhook integration
- No career page analytics dashboard

#### **Mobile & UX**
- Layout appears responsive but not explicitly tested
- No mobile-specific optimizations mentioned
- No progressive web app (PWA) capability
- No offline view
- No job alerts/notifications push capability
- No resume quick-upload on mobile

#### **Accessibility**
- No ARIA labels beyond minimal
- No keyboard navigation enhancements shown
- No color contrast checker integration
- No screen reader testing mentioned

**What Recruiters CAN Customize:**
✅ Company branding (name, logo URL, one color)  
✅ Career page slug/URL  
✅ Tagline & about section  
✅ Activate/deactivate entire career page  
✅ Toggle which jobs are published (on/off per job)  
✅ Set job metadata (location, department, employment type, salary)  
✅ View live career page URL  
✅ Slug availability checking  

**What Recruiters CANNOT Customize:**
❌ Custom CSS/HTML for page  
❌ Supported fields beyond location, department, employment_type, salary  
❌ Email templates or reply-to addresses  
❌ Job categories/tags (beyond department)  
❌ Application form fields (these are per-job but not visible in Career Settings)  
❌ Analytics dashboard  
❌ Application notifications  
❌ Job expiry dates  
❌ Featured/sponsored jobs  
❌ Custom domain  
❌ Visibility to specific teams/accounts  

**Missing Settings Pages:**
- No analytics dashboard
- No application management integration
- No email notification settings
- No social share customization
- No SEO settings per page
- No advanced job metadata fields (benefits, perks, team size, salary history, etc.)

---

### 6. PUBLIC PAGE QUALITY

**Strengths:**
- Clean, modern design with good use of whitespace
- Responsive layout (mobile-first approach visible)
- Smooth interactions (hover effects, transitions)
- Good accessibility structure (semantic HTML, icon + text combinations)
- Professional footer with legal disclaimer
- Smart filtering (only shows filters when relevant)
- Good visual hierarchy
- Social sharing integrated
- Fast load times (uses React Query caching, 60-second stale time)
- Branded colors respected throughout

**Weaknesses & Gaps:**
- Very basic (looks more like a prototype than production career page)
- No rich job descriptions visible on listing page
- No featured section or job spotlight
- No candidate testimonials
- No company culture content
- No team member profiles
- No benefits/perks display
- No application success stories
- No "Why join us" section beyond one about field
- No job detail page (only apply modal routing)
- No SEO for individual jobs
- No engagement metrics ("X+ applications this week")
- Social sharing buttons are subtle/hard to notice
- No "recent applications" or "apply before Friday" urgency signals
- No video/media in career page
- No candidate reviews (Glassdoor-style)
- Not production-grade from an HR perspective

**UX Gaps:**
- No breadcrumb navigation
- Search doesn't show "no results found" messaging for bad matches clearly
- Filters reset when you navigate away
- No "save job" or favorites functionality
- No job email alert signup
- No back button if coming from external link
- No related/similar jobs suggestions after applying
- Filter pills could show active count
- No salary range search (just hardcoded location/department)

---

**Good:**

- Career page config visible to:
  - Unauthenticated users if is_active = true (via get_career_page RPC)
  - Team admins always (for settings)

The 20260408000000 migration fixed a critical bug where only job owners (user_id = auth.uid()) could update jobs, preventing team members from toggling is_published on the career page. Now any team member can update their team's jobs.

## Rankora Tier 1 Feature Deep Audit

**Date:** 2026-04-07
**Reviewer:** Sage
**Scope:** All 10 Tier 1 "must-have" features -- end-to-end data flow verification

---

### Feature 1: AI Candidate Ranking/Shortlisting

**STATUS: COMPLETE**

**What works:**
- Full pipeline verified end-to-end: JD entry --> `analyze-jd` edge function (GPT-4o analysis with structured output: must-haves, dimensions, rubrics) --> file upload to Supabase Storage + resume record creation --> `parse-resume` edge function (multi-method extraction: BT/ET for PDFs, mammoth for DOCX, Gemini OCR fallback, RTF/TXT native) --> `rank-resumes` edge function (dual scoring: rule-based deterministic + GPT deep scoring) --> results stored in `results` table --> polling via `rankAndPoll()` in `JobDetailView.tsx` --> display with `ScoreSummaryCards` + `CandidateRow` components
- JD analysis generates 4-8 evaluation dimensions with rubrics, extracts critical/preferred must-haves, tools, soft skills, inferred priorities
- Dynamic weight generation with 3 strategies: equal, priority_boosted (default), custom admin overrides
- Weight normalization with min 0.05 / max 0.50 clamping, iterative normalization to sum to 1.0
- Fuzzy skill matching with 40+ synonym groups (e.g., "typescript" matches "ts", "kubernetes" matches "k8s")
- Token overlap matching for partial skill matches
- Rule-based scoring covers: skill match, experience fit (with overlapping interval merging), tool match, education fit, must-have coverage
- Must-have penalty system: missing critical must-haves apply score penalty + hard_fit cap (proportional to number missing)
- GPT deep scoring with structured JSON output: per-dimension scores with evidence, strengths, gaps, interview questions
- Automatic retry on all-zero or mostly-zero GPT scores
- JD embedding generation (text-embedding-3-small) for semantic similarity
- Resume embedding generation for vector search capability
- Auth verified: user ownership check on job before ranking
- Configurable model, temperature, system prompts via `ranking_config` table
- Credit deduction before ranking, usage logging

**What's broken:**
- `BATCH_SIZE = 1` at line 23 of `rank-resumes/index.ts` -- resumes are scored sequentially (one at a time), which is slow for large batches. This is a performance concern, not a functional bug.
- `(supabase as any)` casts used in multiple places for fields not in auto-generated types (e.g., `jd_analysis_json`, `dynamic_weights_json`, `jd_embedding`). Functional but bypasses type safety.

**What's missing:**
- Nothing material. This is the strongest feature in the codebase.

**Files involved:**
- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/supabase/functions/analyze-jd/index.ts` (277 lines)
- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/supabase/functions/rank-resumes/index.ts` (700+ lines)
- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/supabase/functions/parse-resume/index.ts` (543 lines)
- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/src/components/JobDetailView.tsx` (1000+ lines)

### Feature 2: Bulk Resume Parsing (200 CVs)

**STATUS: COMPLETE**

**What works:**
- `BulkUploadZone.tsx` is a fully implemented component with `maxFiles = 200` default
- File validation: type allowlist (PDF, DOCX, DOC, RTF, TXT), size limit per file (configurable, default 5MB), duplicate detection by filename
- Concurrency: `CONCURRENCY = 5` -- processes 5 files in parallel batches
- Queue pattern: iterates through pending files in batches, tracks per-file status (pending/uploading/done/failed)
- Cancel support via `cancelRef.current` flag
- Per-file retry and "retry all failed" functionality
- Progress bar showing X/Y uploaded with percentage
- File removal from queue before upload
- Storage path: `{userId}/{jobId}/{timestamp}_{filename}`
- Resume record creation in `resumes` table after storage upload
- Cleanup: if DB insert fails, storage file is removed
- Drag-and-drop support with visual feedback
- Integrated into `JobDetailView.tsx` via `showBulkUpload` toggle with `handleBulkUploadComplete` callback that refreshes the resume list

**What's broken:**
- Nothing functionally broken.

**What's missing:**
- No server-side batch parsing trigger after bulk upload. The `parse-resume` function is called individually per resume during the ranking flow, not immediately after upload. This means bulk-uploaded resumes sit as "pending" until the user triggers ranking. This is by design (parse-on-rank), but users may expect immediate parsing.
- No progress indication during the ranking/parsing phase for 200 resumes (only upload progress is shown).

- Full CRUD: add, edit, delete, reorder (move up/down with DB sort_order persistence)

- Fields stored in `job_form_fields` table per job
- Collapsible UI integrated into `JobDetailView.tsx` per job
- `Apply.tsx` renders custom fields dynamically via `CustomFieldInput` component
- All 8 field types rendered correctly: Input for text/number/url/date, Textarea for textarea, Checkbox for checkbox, Select for select, multi-checkbox group for multiselect

- Accessible: labels with `htmlFor`, `aria-invalid` on error, error messages with `role="alert"`

**What's broken:**

### DB Migration — `supabase/migrations/20260408900000_interview_scheduling.sql`

```sql
-- Recruiter availability slots
CREATE TABLE public.availability_slots (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  team_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.teams(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  day_of_week integer NOT NULL CHECK (day_of_week BETWEEN 0 AND 6), -- 0=Sun, 6=Sat
  start_time time NOT NULL,
  end_time time NOT NULL,
  timezone text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'UTC',
  is_active boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CHECK (start_time < end_time)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_availability_user ON public.availability_slots(user_id, day_of_week);
ALTER TABLE public.availability_slots ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

CREATE POLICY "Users can manage own availability" ON public.availability_slots FOR ALL TO authenticated USING (user_id = auth.uid());
CREATE POLICY "Team members can view team availability" ON public.availability_slots FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (public.is_team_member(auth.uid(), team_id));

-- Scheduled interviews
CREATE TABLE public.interviews (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  job_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.jobs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  resume_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.resumes(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  interviewer_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  candidate_name text NOT NULL,
  candidate_email text,
  scheduled_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
  duration_minutes integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 30,
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'scheduled' CHECK (status IN ('scheduled', 'completed', 'cancelled', 'no_show')),
  meeting_link text,
  notes text,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX idx_interviews_job ON public.interviews(job_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_interviews_interviewer ON public.interviews(interviewer_id, scheduled_at);
ALTER TABLE public.interviews ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

CREATE POLICY "Team can view interviews" ON public.interviews FOR SELECT TO authenticated
  USING (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.jobs j LEFT JOIN public.team_members tm ON tm.team_id = j.team_id AND tm.user_id = auth.uid() WHERE j.id = interviews.job_id AND (j.user_id = auth.uid() OR tm.user_id IS NOT NULL)));

CREATE POLICY "Team can manage interviews" ON public.interviews FOR ALL TO authenticated
  USING (interviewer_id = auth.uid() OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.jobs j WHERE j.id = interviews.job_id AND j.user_id = auth.uid()));

-- Public booking tokens
CREATE TABLE public.booking_tokens (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  job_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.jobs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  resume_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.resumes(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  interviewer_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  token text NOT NULL UNIQUE DEFAULT encode(extensions.gen_random_bytes(24), 'hex'),
  duration_minutes integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 30,
  expires_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT (now() + interval '7 days'),
  used boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

ALTER TABLE public.booking_tokens ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY "Interviewers can create tokens" ON public.booking_tokens FOR ALL TO authenticated USING (interviewer_id = auth.uid());
```

- Props: `candidatePhone, candidateName, jobTitle, messageTemplate?`
- Generates wa.me link: `https://wa.me/${phone}?text=${encodedMessage}`
- Default template: "Hi {name}, regarding your application for {jobTitle} at our company..."
- Opens in new tab

- Routes: GET /jobs, GET /jobs/:id/candidates, GET /jobs/:id/results, POST /jobs

# Landing Page Redesign — Full-Width SaaS Marketing Page

## Context
Current landing page is wrapped in a sidebar layout, max-w-5xl, small headings, no social proof, no product demo. Looks like an internal dashboard, not a SaaS marketing page. Needs a complete rewrite as a standalone full-width page that competes with Manatal, BreezyHR, and top ATS products.

## Approach
Rewrite `src/components/LandingPage.tsx` from scratch. Remove sidebar/AppHeader entirely. Full-width sections with max-w-7xl content. Premium design with gradient hero, mock product UI, competitive pricing, FAQ accordion.

## Key structural change
- Remove: `SidebarProvider`, `SidebarInset`, `JobSidebar`, `AppHeader` imports
- Keep: `AuthDialog` (same signup/signin flow)
- Full-width: no sidebar, sections alternate bg-background and bg-muted
- Sticky nav with scroll-based blur effect

## 11 Sections to build

### 1. Sticky Nav
- Fixed top, transparent → bg-background/80 backdrop-blur on scroll
- Logo + nav links (Features, Pricing, FAQ) + Sign In / Start Free CTAs
- Mobile: Sheet hamburger menu
- `useScrolled()` hook for scroll detection

### 2. Hero
- `pt-32 pb-24` with CSS gradient blobs background (no images)
- Badge: "AI-powered hiring OS — Free to start"
- H1: `text-5xl sm:text-6xl lg:text-7xl` — "Stop reading resumes. Let AI shortlist your best candidates."
- Gradient text on "Let AI shortlist" (primary blue gradient)
- Two CTAs: "Start Free — No Card Needed" (primary) + "See How It Works" (outline, scrolls to #demo)
- Trust bar: No card required / Under 2 min / 500+ recruiters

### 3. Stats Bar
- `bg-muted` alternating section, 4-col grid
- 10,000+ resumes ranked / <2 min screening / 94% accuracy / 500+ teams

### 4. How It Works (3 steps)
- Numbered step cards with connector line between them
- Paste JD → Upload resumes → Get ranked results
- Hover effects on cards

### 5. Features Grid (8 cards)
- `bg-muted` section, 4-col at xl, 3 at lg, 2 at md, 1 at sm
- AI Ranking, Kanban Pipeline, Custom Forms, Team Collab, Career Page, Guest Portal, CSV Import, Auto-Ack

### 6. Product Demo (highest CRO value)
- 2-col layout: left = text + bullet points + CTA, right = mock product UI
- Mock UI: browser chrome frame + 4 candidate rows with scores, skills, stage badges
- Floating cards: "AI insight" + "Time saved 4.2 hrs" (hidden below xl)
- Float animation keyframe needed in tailwind config

### 7. Pricing (4 tiers)
- Monthly/Annual toggle (annual saves 20%)
- Free ($0), Starter ($29), Growth ($79, highlighted), Agency ($149)
- Growth card: border-primary, shadow, "Most Popular" badge
- All CTAs open AuthDialog

### 8. Testimonials (3 cards)
- Realistic placeholder quotes from recruiter personas
- Quote icon + text + avatar + name/role/company

### 9. FAQ (8 items)
- shadcn Accordion, max-w-3xl centered
- Covers: free plan, credits, accuracy, security, team, languages, cancellation, integrations

### 10. Final CTA Banner
- Dark blue gradient background (fixed, not theme-dependent)
- White text, email input + white CTA button (inverted style)
- "Your next great hire is in that pile of resumes."

### 11. Footer
- 4-col: Brand (logo + desc + social) | Product | Company | Legal
- Bottom bar: copyright + "Built by Boldteq"

## Files to modify
- `src/components/LandingPage.tsx` — complete rewrite (single file, ~800 lines)
- `tailwind.config.ts` — add `float` animation keyframe

## Files to verify (no changes needed)
- `src/App.tsx` — already renders `<LandingPage />` when user is null
- `src/components/AuthDialog.tsx` — reused unchanged

## Animations
- FadeIn + StaggerList from `src/components/ui/` (already exist)
- Framer motion staggerChildren for hero sequence
- CSS float keyframe for mock UI floating cards

## Verification
1. `npm run build` — zero TypeScript errors
2. Open `/` in browser (logged out) — full landing page renders
3. Click "Start Free" — AuthDialog opens to signup
4. Click "Sign In" — AuthDialog opens to signin
5. Click nav links — smooth scroll to sections
6. Test mobile hamburger menu
7. Toggle dark mode — all sections adapt
8. Check all responsive breakpoints (xs through xl)

# Tier 2 Differentiators — Build the 3 Missing Features

## Context
Tier 2 audit shows 8 of 11 features already exist. Three gaps remain:
1. **WhatsApp integration** — completely missing, huge differentiator in India/SEA/LATAM/MENA
2. **One-click rejection emails with AI feedback** — only generic email outreach exists
3. **Open API documentation page** — API mentioned in pricing but no docs/playground

## Build Plan

### Feature 1: WhatsApp Integration (via wa.me deep links + Twilio API)

**Approach:** Two tiers — immediate (wa.me deep links, no API needed) + future (Twilio WhatsApp API for automated messages).

**MVP (build now):** wa.me deep links for one-click messaging from candidate cards.

**DB Migration** — `supabase/migrations/20260409000000_whatsapp_and_api.sql`
- Add `whatsapp_number` to `profiles` table (recruiter's WhatsApp number)
- Add `phone` column to `resumes` table if not exists (candidate phone from parsed resume)

**Component** — `src/components/candidate/WhatsAppButton.tsx`
- Props: `candidatePhone, candidateName, jobTitle, messageTemplate?`
- Generates wa.me link: `https://wa.me/${phone}?text=${encodedMessage}`
- Default template: "Hi {name}, regarding your application for {jobTitle} at our company..."
- Opens in new tab
- Shows WhatsApp icon (green) button

**WhatsApp Templates** — `src/components/WhatsAppTemplateManager.tsx`
- Settings component for managing message templates
- Pre-built templates: Interview Invite, Application Update, Document Request, Offer Discussion
- Template variables: `{{candidate_name}}`, `{{job_title}}`, `{{interview_date}}`
- Stored in localStorage initially (no DB needed for MVP)

**Integration points:**
- Add WhatsApp button to `CandidateDetailSheet.tsx` action bar (alongside Email/Call)
- Add WhatsApp button to `CandidateRow.tsx` (if phone number available)
- Add WhatsApp number field to `Settings.tsx` or `Profile.tsx`
- Show in KanbanBoard cards (small icon if phone available)

### Feature 2: One-Click Rejection Emails with AI Feedback

**Edge Function** — `supabase/functions/generate-rejection/index.ts`
- Auth required
- Input: `{ candidate_name, job_title, strengths, gaps, missing_skills }`
- Uses GPT-4o to generate personalized, empathetic rejection email
- Returns: `{ subject, body }` with constructive feedback (what was strong, areas to develop)
- Tone: professional, encouraging, specific — not generic "we regret to inform you"

**Component** — `src/components/candidate/RejectWithFeedbackDialog.tsx`
- Props: `resumeId, jobId, candidateName, candidateEmail, result (scores/gaps/strengths)`
- On open: calls generate-rejection edge function with candidate data
- Shows generated email preview (editable subject + body)
- "Send & Reject" button: sends email via Resend + updates candidate stage to "rejected"
- Loading state during generation
- Option to skip AI and use a simple template

**Integration:**
- Add "Reject with Feedback" button in CandidateDetailSheet
- Add to KanbanBoard — when dropping into "Rejected" column, offer dialog
- Add to ApplicationsTab — status change to "rejected" can trigger the dialog
- Track rejection emails sent in a log

### Feature 3: Open API Documentation Page

**Page** — `src/pages/ApiDocs.tsx`
- Route: `/api-docs` (protected, only visible to users on Growth/Agency plans)
- Sections:
  - Authentication (API key generation + display)
  - Endpoints reference (jobs, candidates, results, applications)
  - Code examples (curl, JavaScript, Python)
  - Webhooks configuration
  - Rate limits

**DB Migration** (in same file `20260409000000_whatsapp_and_api.sql`)
- `api_keys` table: id, user_id, team_id, key_hash (SHA-256), prefix (first 8 chars for display), name, created_at, last_used_at, revoked
- RLS: user can manage own keys

**API Key Management Component** — `src/components/ApiKeyManager.tsx`
- Generate new API key (show once, then only prefix)
- List existing keys with name, prefix, created date, last used
- Revoke keys
- Copy key to clipboard

**Edge Function** — `supabase/functions/public-api/index.ts`
- Validates API key from `Authorization: Bearer rk_...` header
- Routes: GET /jobs, GET /jobs/:id/candidates, GET /jobs/:id/results, POST /jobs
- Returns JSON responses
- Rate limiting: 100 req/min per key

**Webhook Config** — `src/components/WebhookManager.tsx`
- Configure webhook URLs for events: application_received, ranking_complete, stage_changed
- Test webhook button (sends sample payload)
- Stored in DB: `webhook_configs` table

**Integration:**
- Add "API" to sidebar nav (only for Growth/Agency plans)
- Add `/api-docs` route to App.tsx
- Show API key in Settings page for eligible plans

## Files Summary

### New files (13)
- `supabase/migrations/20260409000000_whatsapp_and_api.sql`
- `supabase/functions/generate-rejection/index.ts`
- `supabase/functions/public-api/index.ts`
- `src/components/candidate/WhatsAppButton.tsx`
- `src/components/candidate/RejectWithFeedbackDialog.tsx`
- `src/components/WhatsAppTemplateManager.tsx`
- `src/components/ApiKeyManager.tsx`
- `src/components/WebhookManager.tsx`
- `src/pages/ApiDocs.tsx`

### Modified files
- `src/components/CandidateDetailSheet.tsx` — add WhatsApp + Reject buttons
- `src/components/KanbanBoard.tsx` — rejection dialog on drop to rejected
- `src/components/ApplicationsTab.tsx` — rejection dialog on status change
- `src/components/JobSidebar.tsx` — add API nav item (plan-gated)
- `src/App.tsx` — add /api-docs route
- `src/pages/Settings.tsx` — add WhatsApp number field

## Verification
1. `npm run build` — zero errors
2. Deploy: migration + 2 edge functions (generate-rejection, public-api)
3. WhatsApp: click button → wa.me link opens with pre-filled message
4. Rejection: generate → preview → send → candidate stage updates
5. API docs: page renders, key generation works, endpoints documented

```sql
CREATE TABLE public.candidate_tags (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  resume_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.resumes(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  job_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.jobs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  tag text NOT NULL,
  color text NOT NULL DEFAULT '#6366f1',
  created_by uuid REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,

I need to: (1) call `useCandidateTags`, (2) build an assignee map, (3) thread data through to `CandidateRow`, `CandidateDetailSheet`, and `KanbanBoard`.

---

## Plan: ZIP Upload + Candidate Tags + Candidate Assignment

### What gets built

**Feature 1: ZIP Upload**
Users can drag/drop or select a `.zip` file in both the regular upload zone and the BulkUploadZone. The app extracts resume files client-side using jszip (dynamically imported to avoid bundle bloat), filters for PDF/DOCX/DOC/RTF/TXT files, and adds them to the upload queue exactly like individually-selected files. Non-resume files inside the zip are silently skipped with a toast summary.

**Feature 2: Candidate Tags**
Free-form text tags per candidate (scoped to a resume+job pair). Stored in a new `candidate_tags` table. Tags appear as small chips inline in CandidateRow (max 3 visible, "+N more" overflow). Full editing (add/remove) happens in the CandidateDetailSheet. Backed by a `useCandidateTags` hook with optimistic updates and the same graceful-fallback pattern used in `useStageTracker`.

**Feature 3: Candidate Assignment**
Assign a team member to a candidate. Stored in `candidate_assignments` table. Shows the assignee's avatar inline in CandidateRow. The full assign/unassign selector (popover listing team members) lives in CandidateDetailSheet. Only visible when a team exists (`useTeam()` returns a team). Backed by a `useCandidateAssignments` hook with optimistic updates.

---

### 11 Steps

| Step | Action | Verifiable output |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `npm install jszip` | `npm run build` passes |
| 2 | Write migration SQL | File exists in `supabase/migrations/` |
| 3 | Create `useCandidateTags.ts` hook | TypeScript compiles |
| 4 | Create `useCandidateAssignments.ts` hook | TypeScript compiles |
| 5 | Create `CandidateTagsEditor.tsx` | Renders chips + input |
| 6 | Create `CandidateAssignMenu.tsx` | Renders popover with team list |
| 7 | Modify `BulkUploadZone.tsx` for ZIP | ZIP accepted, entries extracted |
| 8 | Modify `JobDetailView.tsx` regular upload for ZIP | ZIP files get extracted before `addFiles()` |
| 9 | Modify `CandidateRow.tsx` — show tags + assignee | Row renders new data without layout break |
| 10 | Modify `CandidateDetailSheet.tsx` — full editors | Tags/assignment fully editable in sheet |
| 11 | Wire hooks in `JobDetailView.tsx` + final build | `npm run build` exits 0, zero TypeScript errors |

---

### Files created (5 new)
- `supabase/migrations/20260410000000_candidate_tags_and_assignments.sql`
- `src/hooks/useCandidateTags.ts`
- `src/hooks/useCandidateAssignments.ts`
- `src/components/candidate/CandidateTagsEditor.tsx`
- `src/components/candidate/CandidateAssignMenu.tsx`

### Files modified (5 existing)

- `src/components/JobDetailView.tsx`
- `src/components/CandidateRow.tsx`

- Tags capped at 10 per candidate, 30 chars each — no unbounded growth
- Assignment hidden when team is null — no broken UI for solo users
- Zero new state management libraries — hooks use React Query patterns already in the app

Build 5 features for Rankora at `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora`. Read CLAUDE.md first.

## Feature 1: AI Resume Authenticity Scoring (MOAT)

Detect AI-generated or fake resumes. This is a 2026 killer feature — flood of ChatGPT-written CVs.

### Edge Function — `supabase/functions/check-authenticity/index.ts`
Copy auth/CORS pattern from `rewrite-jd/index.ts`. Auth required, no credit deduction.

Input: `{ resume_text: string, candidate_name: string }`

System prompt: "You are an expert resume fraud analyst. Analyze this resume for signs of AI generation or fabrication. Check for: (1) generic/templated language patterns typical of ChatGPT, (2) inconsistent dates or experience gaps, (3) implausible skill combinations, (4) buzzword stuffing without specifics, (5) formatting anomalies, (6) claims that seem fabricated. Return a JSON object."

Output:
```json
{
  "authenticity_score": 85,
  "risk_level": "low",
  "flags": ["Generic project descriptions", "Some buzzword clustering"],
  "details": { "ai_generated_likelihood": 15, "inconsistency_count": 0, "buzzword_density": "moderate" },
  "summary": "This resume appears largely authentic with minor templated language..."
}
```

### Component — `src/components/candidate/AuthenticityBadge.tsx`
Small badge showing authenticity score. Props: `score: number | null, riskLevel: string`
- Green shield (score >= 80): "Verified"
- Amber shield (60-79): "Review"  
- Red shield (< 60): "Risk"
- Null: "Not checked"
- Tooltip shows details on hover

### Component — `src/components/candidate/AuthenticityReport.tsx`
Full report card. Props: `resumeId, jobId`
- Fetches from a `resume_authenticity` column on results or a separate table
- Score ring, risk level, flag list, detailed breakdown, AI summary
- "Run Check" button if not yet analyzed

### Integration
- Add AuthenticityBadge to CandidateRow (next to score)
- Add AuthenticityReport to CandidateDetailSheet
- Add "Check Authenticity" button to CandidateDetailSheet actions
- Store results: add `authenticity_json` column to `results` table in migration

## Feature 2: Stage-Triggered Automation

When a candidate moves to a stage, automatically perform actions (send email, assign task, etc).

### DB Migration — `supabase/migrations/20260410100000_automation_and_features.sql`

```sql
-- Stage automation rules
CREATE TABLE public.stage_automations (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  team_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.teams(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  stage_name text NOT NULL,
  action_type text NOT NULL CHECK (action_type IN ('send_email', 'create_task', 'add_tag', 'notify_team')),
  action_config jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  is_active boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
ALTER TABLE public.stage_automations ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY "Team members view" ON public.stage_automations FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (public.is_team_member(auth.uid(), team_id));
CREATE POLICY "Team admins manage" ON public.stage_automations FOR ALL TO authenticated USING (public.is_team_admin(auth.uid(), team_id));

-- Authenticity results storage
ALTER TABLE public.results ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS authenticity_json jsonb;

-- Talent pool
CREATE TABLE public.talent_pool (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  team_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.teams(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  resume_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.resumes(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  original_job_id uuid REFERENCES public.jobs(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  added_by uuid REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  notes text,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE(team_id, resume_id)
);
ALTER TABLE public.talent_pool ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY "Team members view pool" ON public.talent_pool FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (public.is_team_member(auth.uid(), team_id));
CREATE POLICY "Team members manage pool" ON public.talent_pool FOR ALL TO authenticated USING (public.is_team_member(auth.uid(), team_id));
```

### Component — `src/components/StageAutomationManager.tsx`
Props: `teamId: string`

Show on Team page. List of automation rules per stage.
- "Add Rule" button → form: Stage (dropdown from custom stages), Action (send_email / create_task / add_tag / notify_team), Config (email template for send_email, task title for create_task, tag name for add_tag)
- List existing rules with toggle active/inactive, delete
- When a candidate's stage changes (in useStageTracker), check for matching automations and execute them client-side (call the appropriate action)

## Feature 3: Talent Pool + Candidate Rediscovery

Save good candidates for future jobs. Re-rank them against new JDs.

### Component — `src/pages/TalentPool.tsx`
Route: `/talent-pool`, protected, SidebarLayout, max-w-5xl.

- Shows all candidates in the talent pool for the team
- Table: Name, Original Job, Score, Skills (from parsed_json), Date Added, Actions
- "Re-rank against new JD" button → opens a dialog where you paste a JD, selects talent pool candidates, and submits them for ranking against the new JD
- Search by name/skills
- Remove from pool button

### Component — `src/components/candidate/AddToPoolButton.tsx`
Small button in CandidateDetailSheet. "Save to Talent Pool" → inserts into talent_pool table.

### Integration
- Add to sidebar nav: "Talent Pool" (Database icon)
- Add route in App.tsx
- Add AddToPoolButton to CandidateDetailSheet

## Feature 4: Incognito / Bias-Blind Mode

Hide candidate PII (name, gender indicators, ethnicity, age, photo) during initial screening.

### Implementation (no DB changes needed — purely UI toggle)

Add a toggle in JobDetailView: "Bias-Blind Mode" (Eye/EyeOff icon).

When active:
- CandidateRow shows "Candidate #1", "Candidate #2" instead of real names
- CandidateDetailSheet hides name, email, phone, LinkedIn — shows "Candidate #X"
- KanbanBoard cards show "Candidate #X"
- Score, skills, experience, education still visible (that's the point — evaluate on merit)

State: `blindMode` boolean in JobDetailView, passed as prop to children. Simple — just conditionally render anonymized names.

## Feature 5: AI-Powered Natural Language Search

Search candidates using natural language: "Find React developers with 5+ years in Bangalore"

### Component — `src/components/AICandidateSearch.tsx`
A search dialog/bar that uses AI to interpret natural language queries.

Props: `jobId?: string` (optional — search within job or across all)

Flow:
1. User types natural language query
2. Call an edge function that converts the query to filters
3. Execute filtered search against resumes/results
4. Display matching candidates

### Edge Function — `supabase/functions/ai-search/index.ts`
Auth required. Input: `{ query: string, job_id?: string }`

Use GPT-4o to parse the query into structured filters:
```json
{
  "skills": ["React", "TypeScript"],
  "min_experience_years": 5,
  "location": "Bangalore",
  "min_score": null
}
```

Then query resumes table with those filters (text search on parsed_text + parsed_json fields).

Return matched candidates.

### Integration

- Search results link to the candidate detail

## Feature 1: AI Resume Authenticity Scoring (MOAT)

Detect AI-generated or fake resumes. This is a 2026 killer feature — flood of ChatGPT-written CVs.

### Edge Function — `supabase/functions/check-authenticity/index.ts`
Copy auth/CORS pattern from `rewrite-jd/index.ts`. Auth required, no credit deduction.

Input: `{ resume_text: string, candidate_name: string }`

System prompt: "You are an expert resume fraud analyst. Analyze this resume for signs of AI generation or fabrication. Check for: (1) generic/templated language patterns typical of ChatGPT, (2) inconsistent dates or experience gaps, (3) implausible skill combinations, (4) buzzword stuffing without specifics, (5) formatting anomalies, (6) claims that seem fabricated. Return a JSON object."

Output:
```json
{
  "authenticity_score": 85,
  "risk_level": "low",
  "flags": ["Generic project descriptions", "Some buzzword clustering"],
  "details": { "ai_generated_likelihood": 15, "inconsistency_count": 0, "buzzword_density": "moderate" },
  "summary": "This resume appears largely authentic with minor templated language..."
}
```

### Component — `src/components/candidate/AuthenticityBadge.tsx`
Small badge showing authenticity score. Props: `score: number | null, riskLevel: string`
- Green shield (score >= 80): "Verified"
- Amber shield (60-79): "Review"  
- Red shield (< 60): "Risk"
- Null: "Not checked"
- Tooltip shows details on hover

### Component — `src/components/candidate/AuthenticityReport.tsx`
Full report card. Props: `resumeId, jobId`
- Fetches from a `resume_authenticity` column on results or a separate table
- Score ring, risk level, flag list, detailed breakdown, AI summary
- "Run Check" button if not yet analyzed

### Integration
- Add AuthenticityBadge to CandidateRow (next to score)
- Add AuthenticityReport to CandidateDetailSheet
- Add "Check Authenticity" button to CandidateDetailSheet actions
- Store results: add `authenticity_json` column to `results` table in migration

## Feature 2: Stage-Triggered Automation

When a candidate moves to a stage, automatically perform actions (send email, assign task, etc).

### DB Migration — `supabase/migrations/20260410100000_automation_and_features.sql`

```sql
-- Stage automation rules
CREATE TABLE public.stage_automations (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  team_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.teams(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  stage_name text NOT NULL,
  action_type text NOT NULL CHECK (action_type IN ('send_email', 'create_task', 'add_tag', 'notify_team')),
  action_config jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  is_active boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
ALTER TABLE public.stage_automations ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY "Team members view" ON public.stage_automations FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (public.is_team_member(auth.uid(), team_id));
CREATE POLICY "Team admins manage" ON public.stage_automations FOR ALL TO authenticated USING (public.is_team_admin(auth.uid(), team_id));

-- Authenticity results storage
ALTER TABLE public.results ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS authenticity_json jsonb;

-- Talent pool
CREATE TABLE public.talent_pool (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  team_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.teams(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  resume_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.resumes(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  original_job_id uuid REFERENCES public.jobs(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  added_by uuid REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  notes text,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE(team_id, resume_id)
);
ALTER TABLE public.talent_pool ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY "Team members view pool" ON public.talent_pool FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (public.is_team_member(auth.uid(), team_id));
CREATE POLICY "Team members manage pool" ON public.talent_pool FOR ALL TO authenticated USING (public.is_team_member(auth.uid(), team_id));
```

### Component — `src/components/StageAutomationManager.tsx`
Props: `teamId: string`

Show on Team page. List of automation rules per stage.
- "Add Rule" button → form: Stage (dropdown from custom stages), Action (send_email / create_task / add_tag / notify_team), Config (email template for send_email, task title for create_task, tag name for add_tag)
- List existing rules with toggle active/inactive, delete
- When a candidate's stage changes (in useStageTracker), check for matching automations and execute them client-side (call the appropriate action)

Save good candidates for future jobs. Re-rank them against new JDs.

### Component — `src/pages/TalentPool.tsx`
Route: `/talent-pool`, protected, SidebarLayout, max-w-5xl.

- Shows all candidates in the talent pool for the team
- Table: Name, Original Job, Score, Skills (from parsed_json), Date Added, Actions
- "Re-rank against new JD" button → opens a dialog where you paste a JD, selects talent pool candidates, and submits them for ranking against the new JD

- Remove from pool button

Hide candidate PII (name, gender indicators, ethnicity, age, photo) during initial screening.

- CandidateDetailSheet hides name, email, phone, LinkedIn — shows "Candidate #X"

- Score, skills, experience, education still visible (that's the point — evaluate on merit)

## Feature 5: AI-Powered Natural Language Search

Search candidates using natural language: "Find React developers with 5+ years in Bangalore"

### Component — `src/components/AICandidateSearch.tsx`
A search dialog/bar that uses AI to interpret natural language queries.

Props: `jobId?: string` (optional — search within job or across all)

Flow:
1. User types natural language query
2. Call an edge function that converts the query to filters
3. Execute filtered search against resumes/results
4. Display matching candidates

### Edge Function — `supabase/functions/ai-search/index.ts`
Auth required. Input: `{ query: string, job_id?: string }`

Use GPT-4o to parse the query into structured filters:
```json
{
  "skills": ["React", "TypeScript"],
  "min_experience_years": 5,
  "location": "Bangalore",
  "min_score": null
}
```

Then query resumes table with those filters (text search on parsed_text + parsed_json fields).

Return matched candidates.

### Integration

## Integrations Audit Report for Rankora

Based on a thorough audit of the codebase at `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora`, here's the complete state of integrations, API keys, and webhooks:

---

### **1. INTEGRATIONS UI STRUCTURE**

#### User-Facing Integrations Page
**File:** `/src/pages/Integrations.tsx`
- Public marketplace of third-party integrations
- Shows 9 integrations across "Available" and "Coming Soon" sections
- **Available integrations (6):**
  - LinkedIn (import candidates, post jobs)
  - Slack (notifications)
  - Google Calendar (interview scheduling)
  - Zapier (5,000+ app automation)
  - Indeed (resume import)
  - Google Workspace (Gmail, Drive, Contacts)
- **Coming Soon (3):**
  - Microsoft Teams
  - Greenhouse ATS
  - Workday
- Uses `IntegrationCard` component with status badges (Available/Coming Soon/Connected)
- Currently all "Connect" buttons are placeholders that show "coming soon" toasts

#### Admin Integrations Tab
**File:** `/src/components/admin/IntegrationsTab.tsx` (837 lines)
- Expandable collapsible cards for each integration
- Integrations managed:
  1. **OpenAI** (GPT-4o for resume ranking & JD analysis)
     - API credential: `OPENAI_API_KEY` (Supabase Edge Function Secret)
     - Used by Edge Functions: `rank-resumes`, `analyze-jd`, `evaluate-model`
     - Test connection available
  2. **Google Gemini** (Gemini 2.0 Flash for OCR fallback)
     - API credential: `GEMINI_API_KEY` (Supabase Edge Function Secret)
     - Used by: `rank-resumes`
     - Fallback for scanned/image-based PDFs
  3. **Resend** (Transactional email service)
     - API credential: `RESEND_API_KEY` (Supabase Edge Function Secret)
     - Editable config: `email_from_address`, `email_from_name`, `inbound_email_domain`
     - Email notifications toggles: ranking complete, resume received
     - Used by: `send-email`, `send-candidate-email`, `email-ingest`
  4. **Dodo Payments** (Payment processing)
     - API credential: `DODO_PAYMENTS_API_KEY` (Supabase Edge Function Secret)
     - Webhook secret: `DODO_PAYMENTS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`
     - Environment mode: test_mode or live_mode (affects all API calls)
     - Webhook endpoint: `{VITE_SUPABASE_URL}/functions/v1/dodo-webhook`
     - Used by: `create-dodo-checkout`, `verify-dodo-payment`, `cancel-dodo-subscription`, `dodo-webhook`, `manage-dodo-product`
  5. **Chat Widget** (Intercom, Crisp, Tawk.to, etc.)
     - Enable toggle + custom embed code textarea
     - Stores in `platform_config` table as `chat_widget_enabled` and `chat_widget_code`
     - Injected on all pages when enabled

---

### **2. API KEYS & WEBHOOK MANAGEMENT**

#### User-Facing API Keys Card
**File:** `/src/components/settings/ApiKeysCard.tsx`
- **Location:** `/api-docs` page, "API Keys" tab
- **API Keys Management:**
  - Generate new keys with optional label (default: "My API Key")
  - Key format: `rk_live_` prefix + 32 random alphanumeric chars
  - Display: masked (first 12 + last 4 chars visible), toggle reveal
  - Operations: Copy, Eye toggle, Delete
  - Storage: localStorage under key `rankora_api_keys` (JSON array)
  - Each key has: id (UUID), label, full key string, createdAt timestamp

- **Webhooks Management:**
  - Register custom webhook URLs (user-provided endpoints)
  - Available events (hardcoded): job.created, ranking.completed, candidate.applied, candidate.rejected, interview.scheduled
  - Default event on creation: `ranking.completed`
  - Active/inactive status indicator (green dot when active)
  - Storage: localStorage under key `rankora_webhooks` (JSON array)
  - Each webhook has: id (UUID), url, events array, active boolean
  - Validation: URL format check
  - Operations: Add, Remove
  - **Note:** This is a frontend-only implementation—no backend persistence

- **API Quick Reference Card:**
  - Shows basic endpoints (GET /api/v1/jobs, POST /api/v1/jobs, etc.)
  - Authentication format: `Authorization: Bearer rk_live_...`

#### API Documentation Page
**File:** `/src/pages/ApiDocs.tsx`
- Three tabs: Reference, API Keys, Quickstart
- **Reference tab:**
  - Base URL: `https://zkzontawprihrzpayeam.supabase.co/functions/v1/public-api`
  - Authentication (Bearer token required)
  - Rate limits: 100 req/min, 50 jobs/day, 500 candidates/response
  - Error codes (400, 401, 404, 405, 429, 500)
  - Endpoints (4 total):
    - GET /jobs (list all)
    - GET /jobs/:id (single job)
    - POST /jobs (create)
    - GET /jobs/:id/candidates (ranked candidates)
- **API Keys tab:** Renders `<ApiKeysCard />`
- **Quickstart tab:**
  - 3-step setup guide
  - Code samples in cURL, JavaScript, Python
  - Webhook quickstart mentioning event types and HMAC-SHA256 signing

---

### **3. ADMIN INTEGRATIONS TAB DATA SOURCES**

**Supabase Tables:**

1. **`integrations`** (read-only metadata)
   - Fields: id, key_name, display_name, description, is_configured, last_test_status, last_tested_at, created_at, updated_at
   - Stores: OpenAI, Gemini, Resend, Dodo status metadata
   - Query: `SELECT * FROM integrations` (order by created_at)
   - Test invocation: calls `admin-test-integration` Edge Function

2. **`platform_config`** (singleton config table)
   - Fields: id, resend_api_key (null), resend_inbound_webhook_secret (null), email_from_address, email_from_name, outbound_email_enabled, email_notify_ranking_complete, email_notify_resume_received, inbound_email_domain, dodo_payments_environment (test_mode|live_mode), dodo_brand_id, chat_widget_enabled, chat_widget_code, booking_embed_url, payg_per_resume_cost, topup_dodo_product_id, topup_min_amount, email_ingestion_enabled, email_notify_bonus_credits, max_resumes_per_job, max_file_size_mb, resume_retention_days, updated_at
   - Query: `.select("*").limit(1).single()` (always single row)
   - Updates: Resend, Dodo, Chat Widget settings saved here

3. **`subscription_webhooks`** (payment webhook log)
   - Fields: id, created_at, event_type, gateway (resend|dodo|razorpay), payload (JSON), processed (boolean), webhook_id, user_id, dodo_subscription_id, razorpay_subscription_id, razorpay_payment_id
   - Stores: Incoming webhook events from payment providers
   - No direct user management UI (admin-only logging)

---

### **4. ROUTE & NAVIGATION INTEGRATION**

**Routes:**

# Tier 2 Differentiators — Build the 3 Missing Features

## Context
Tier 2 audit shows 8 of 11 features already exist. Three gaps remain:
1. **WhatsApp integration** — completely missing, huge differentiator in India/SEA/LATAM/MENA
2. **One-click rejection emails with AI feedback** — only generic email outreach exists
3. **Open API documentation page** — API mentioned in pricing but no docs/playground

## Build Plan

### Feature 1: WhatsApp Integration (via wa.me deep links + Twilio API)

**Approach:** Two tiers — immediate (wa.me deep links, no API needed) + future (Twilio WhatsApp API for automated messages).

**MVP (build now):** wa.me deep links for one-click messaging from candidate cards.

**DB Migration** — `supabase/migrations/20260409000000_whatsapp_and_api.sql`
- Add `whatsapp_number` to `profiles` table (recruiter's WhatsApp number)
- Add `phone` column to `resumes` table if not exists (candidate phone from parsed resume)

**Component** — `src/components/candidate/WhatsAppButton.tsx`
- Props: `candidatePhone, candidateName, jobTitle, messageTemplate?`
- Generates wa.me link: `https://wa.me/${phone}?text=${encodedMessage}`
- Default template: "Hi {name}, regarding your application for {jobTitle} at our company..."
- Opens in new tab
- Shows WhatsApp icon (green) button

**WhatsApp Templates** — `src/components/WhatsAppTemplateManager.tsx`
- Settings component for managing message templates
- Pre-built templates: Interview Invite, Application Update, Document Request, Offer Discussion
- Template variables: `{{candidate_name}}`, `{{job_title}}`, `{{interview_date}}`

The auth logic looks correct — it queries `user_roles` table for the admin role. If you're getting redirected away from `/admin`, it means either:
1. The `user_roles` table doesn't have your user with role `admin`, OR
2. The `isAdmin` check runs before the role fetch completes

Let me check for a race condition — the `AdminRoute` checks `isAdmin` but the role fetch is async and happens in a `setTimeout`:

Found the race condition. Line 88: `setLoading(false)` runs BEFORE `fetchRole` completes (since `fetchRole` is async). This means:

1. `getSession()` fires → sets user → calls `fetchRole()` (async, takes time)
2. `setLoading(false)` runs immediately (doesn't await fetchRole)
3. `AdminRoute` sees `loading=false`, `isAdmin=false` (role hasn't loaded yet)
4. Redirects to `/` because `isAdmin` is still false

The fix: don't set `loading` to false until BOTH profile and role are fetched.

content.text:
Fixed. The root cause was a **race condition** in `useAuth.tsx`:

1. `getSession()` found a valid session
2. Called `fetchRole(userId)` (async, takes ~100ms to hit Supabase)
3. Immediately called `setLoading(false)` **without awaiting** the role fetch
4. `AdminRoute` saw `loading=false` + `isAdmin=false` → redirected to `/`

**Fix:** `await Promise.all([fetchProfile(), fetchRole()])` before `setLoading(false)`. Now the auth loading state stays true until both profile AND admin role are resolved, so `AdminRoute` sees the correct `isAdmin` value.

content.text:
Here is the complete plan:

---

## Plan: Profile Page Redesign

### Files to create/modify

**1. `supabase/migrations/20260410200000_profile_fields.sql`** (new file)

11 `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` statements on `public.profiles`:
- `full_name`, `username`, `bio`, `avatar_url` (personal)
- `job_title`, `company`, `location` (work)
- `website`, `twitter`, `linkedin`, `github` (social)

All `text` type, all nullable.

**2. `src/pages/Profile.tsx`** (full rewrite)

---

### Architecture decisions

**Data loading strategy (key decision):**
The `useAuth` profile context only fetches a fixed set of columns and I must not modify `types.ts`. So instead of touching useAuth, the page will run its own dedicated React Query (`queryKey: ["profileFull", user?.id]`) that fetches the new columns via `(supabase as any)`. The form populates from that query. After save, `queryClient.invalidateQueries(["profileFull"])` + `refreshProfile()` to sync credits.

**Input prefix addon pattern:**
A raw `<input>` nested inside a styled wrapper div (not shadcn `<Input>`) to achieve the "twitter.com/ [handle]" visual grouping without fighting shadcn's border/ring on a sibling element. The wrapper div carries the border and focus ring.

---

### Page sections (top to bottom inside main Card)

| # | Section | Components |
|---|---------|-----------|
| 1 | Avatar | Circle (img or initials), Upload button, Remove button, hidden file input |
| 2 | Personal Information | Separator + label, 2-col grid: Full Name, Username (@prefix), Email (disabled), Member Since (static text), Bio (full-width Textarea, 160-char counter) |
| 3 | Work Details | Separator + label, 2-col grid: Job Title, Company, Location (full width) |
| 4 | Social Links | Separator + label, 2-col grid: Website (https://), Twitter (twitter.com/), LinkedIn (linkedin.com/in/), GitHub (github.com/) |
| 5 | Plan & Usage | Separator + label, badge row (plan + credits + subscription), 3 stat cards (jobs/resumes/credits used) with Skeleton while loading |
| 6 | Action buttons | Cancel (outline, resets form) + Save Changes (primary, disabled+spinner while saving) |

Below the card: `<ChangePasswordCard />` unchanged.

---

### Avatar upload flow
1. Hidden `<input type="file" accept="image/*" ref={fileInputRef}>`
2. Upload button calls `fileInputRef.current?.click()`
3. `onChange` handler: upload file to Supabase Storage bucket `avatars` at `{user.id}/{filename}`, get public URL, update `form.avatar_url` and immediately save to DB, call `toast.success`
4. Remove button: deletes from storage (best-effort), sets `form.avatar_url = ""`, saves null to DB

---

### handleSave / handleCancel
- Save: `(supabase as any).from("profiles").update({ ...form }).eq("user_id", user.id)`, then `queryClient.invalidateQueries(["profileFull"])` + `refreshProfile()`, then `toast.success("Profile updated")`
- Cancel: reset form state to `fullProfile` values (same as the `useEffect` on load)

---

### Risk mitigations
- **Storage bucket may not exist:** wrapped in try-catch, descriptive toast error
- **New columns not in types.ts:** all accesses use `(supabase as any)` — zero type conflicts
- **useAuth not touched:** separate React Query for new columns; useAuth only called for `user`, `profile` (credits/plan), `refreshProfile`

---

### Build order
1. Write migration SQL file
2. Write new Profile.tsx
3. `npm run build` — zero errors
4. Confirm `types.ts` is untouched

Here is the complete plan:

---

## Plan: Profile Page Redesign

### Files to create/modify

**1. `supabase/migrations/20260410200000_profile_fields.sql`** (new file)

11 `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` statements on `public.profiles`:
- `full_name`, `username`, `bio`, `avatar_url` (personal)
- `job_title`, `company`, `location` (work)
- `website`, `twitter`, `linkedin`, `github` (social)

All `text` type, all nullable.

**2. `src/pages/Profile.tsx`** (full rewrite)

---

### Architecture decisions

**Data loading strategy (key decision):**
The `useAuth` profile context only fetches a fixed set of columns and I must not modify `types.ts`. So instead of touching useAuth, the page will run its own dedicated React Query (`queryKey: ["profileFull", user?.id]`) that fetches the new columns via `(supabase as any)`. The form populates from that query. After save, `queryClient.invalidateQueries(["profileFull"])` + `refreshProfile()` to sync credits.

**Input prefix addon pattern:**
A raw `<input>` nested inside a styled wrapper div (not shadcn `<Input>`) to achieve the "twitter.com/ [handle]" visual grouping without fighting shadcn's border/ring on a sibling element. The wrapper div carries the border and focus ring.

---

### Page sections (top to bottom inside main Card)

| # | Section | Components |
|---|---------|-----------|
| 1 | Avatar | Circle (img or initials), Upload button, Remove button, hidden file input |
| 2 | Personal Information | Separator + label, 2-col grid: Full Name, Username (@prefix), Email (disabled), Member Since (static text), Bio (full-width Textarea, 160-char counter) |
| 3 | Work Details | Separator + label, 2-col grid: Job Title, Company, Location (full width) |
| 4 | Social Links | Separator + label, 2-col grid: Website (https://), Twitter (twitter.com/), LinkedIn (linkedin.com/in/), GitHub (github.com/) |
| 5 | Plan & Usage | Separator + label, badge row (plan + credits + subscription), 3 stat cards (jobs/resumes/credits used) with Skeleton while loading |
| 6 | Action buttons | Cancel (outline, resets form) + Save Changes (primary, disabled+spinner while saving) |

Below the card: `<ChangePasswordCard />` unchanged.

---

### Avatar upload flow
1. Hidden `<input type="file" accept="image/*" ref={fileInputRef}>`
2. Upload button calls `fileInputRef.current?.click()`
3. `onChange` handler: upload file to Supabase Storage bucket `avatars` at `{user.id}/{filename}`, get public URL, update `form.avatar_url` and immediately save to DB, call `toast.success`
4. Remove button: deletes from storage (best-effort), sets `form.avatar_url = ""`, saves null to DB

---

### handleSave / handleCancel
- Save: `(supabase as any).from("profiles").update({ ...form }).eq("user_id", user.id)`, then `queryClient.invalidateQueries(["profileFull"])` + `refreshProfile()`, then `toast.success("Profile updated")`
- Cancel: reset form state to `fullProfile` values (same as the `useEffect` on load)

---

### Risk mitigations
- **Storage bucket may not exist:** wrapped in try-catch, descriptive toast error
- **New columns not in types.ts:** all accesses use `(supabase as any)` — zero type conflicts
- **useAuth not touched:** separate React Query for new columns; useAuth only called for `user`, `profile` (credits/plan), `refreshProfile`

---

### Build order
1. Write migration SQL file
2. Write new Profile.tsx
3. `npm run build` — zero errors
4. Confirm `types.ts` is untouched

Ready to execute on your go.

content.text:
Perfect. Now I have a complete picture of the Rankora codebase. Let me compile the audit report:

---

## HR Roadmap v5 Audit Report - Rankora

### FEATURE 1: TASKS ✅ **MOSTLY COMPLETE**

**File:** `/src/pages/Tasks.tsx` | `/src/hooks/useTasks.tsx`

**WHAT EXISTS:**
- ✅ Create tasks with **title** (required), **description**, **due_date**, **priority** (low/medium/high)
- ✅ **Assign to single recruiter** (assigned_to field)
- ✅ **Status flow:** todo → in_progress → done (tri-state support)
- ✅ **Collaboration:** Team-scoped (team_id), visible to all team members, created_by tracking
- ✅ Overdue/Due Soon/Upcoming sections with visual badges
- ✅ Completed tasks section (collapsible)
- ✅ Delete permissions (creator or admin only)
- ✅ Real-time updates via Supabase channels
- ✅ Priority visual indicators with color coding
- ✅ Assignee avatars showing assigned member

**NEEDS WORK:**
- ❌ **Assign MULTIPLE recruiters** — only single `assigned_to` field exists. Would need many-to-many table for multi-assignment.
- ❌ **Comments/collaboration thread** on tasks — no discussion capability
- ❌ **Activity tracking** for task changes (who updated, when) — basic created_at/updated_at but no audit log

**Status:** Feature mostly functional but missing multi-assign and task collaboration threads.

---

### FEATURE 2: TALENT POOL ✅ **FUNCTIONAL**

**File:** `/src/pages/TalentPool.tsx` | `/src/hooks/useCandidateTags.tsx`

**WHAT EXISTS:**
- ✅ **Add candidates** from job rankings to talent pool (via talent_pool table with resume_id)
- ✅ **Tag/categorize** — `candidate_tags` table supports tagging by job + resume
- ✅ **Search/filter** by name, location, or original job title
- ✅ **Assign to job** — pool entries track original_job_id for context
- ✅ **Archive** (soft-delete) candidates from pool
- ✅ **Notes** on each candidate (internal notes field, editable)
- ✅ **Scores** displayed (overall_score, skill_score, experience_score from results table)
- ✅ **Authenticity badge** (risk flagging with summary)
- ✅ **Added date** and **added_by** tracking

**NEEDS WORK:**
- ❌ **Bulk operations** (archive/add multiple at once) — UI only supports single-item operations
- ❌ **Export functionality** — no CSV/bulk export of pool

**Status:** Feature complete for individual candidate management. Good MVP. Bulk ops would be next iteration.

---

### FEATURE 3: ACTIVITY ✅ **FUNCTIONAL WITH REALTIME**

**File:** `/src/pages/Activity.tsx` | `/src/hooks/useActivityFeed.tsx`

**WHAT EXISTS:**
- ✅ **Activity timeline** showing team events in reverse chronological order
- ✅ **Filter tabs:** All, Tasks, Notes, Stages, Applications, Members
- ✅ **Real-time:** Supabase subscription on `activity_log` table (postgres_changes)
- ✅ **Notifications:** Activity feed acts as live notification center
- ✅ **Audit storage:** activity_log table with actor_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, metadata, created_at
- ✅ **Pagination:** "Load more" button with 50-item pages
- ✅ **No team state** — shows empty state if not in team

**NEEDS WORK:**
- ❌ **Granular permission checks** — activity feed doesn't filter by who can view (shows all team activity)
- ❌ **Email/notification push** — activity stored but no email/push alerts configured
- ❌ **Detailed metadata** — metadata field is generic; could expand with richer context

**Status:** Activity feed is solid. Good foundation for notifications/auditing. Email/push alerts would be Phase 2.

---

### FEATURE 4: TEAM HUB (Should merge Team + Activity) ❌ **SEPARATE PAGES**

**Files:** `/src/pages/Team.tsx` (Team management) | `/src/pages/Activity.tsx` (Activity feed)

**CURRENT STATE:**
- **Team.tsx** = Member management (invite/roles/remove), Stats (jobs/candidates/tasks/members), Recent Activity preview, Task summary by assignee
- **Activity.tsx** = Full activity timeline with filters
- **They ARE separate pages** but Team.tsx shows "Recent Activity" section (3-item preview)

**ANALYSIS:**
The **HR Roadmap v5 recommends merging these into "Team Hub" with tabs** (Overview + Members + Settings + Activity). Currently:

- ✅ Team already has tabs: **Overview | Members | Settings**
- ❌ **Activity is NOT a tab in Team.tsx** — it's a separate page at `/activity`
- ❌ Recommended structure: Team Hub with tabs = [Overview, Members, Settings, **Activity**]

**NEEDS WORK:**
- Move Activity.tsx into Team.tsx as a 4th tab
- Route `/team` becomes the unified Team Hub
- Keep `/activity` for backward compatibility or redirect to `/team?tab=activity`
- This consolidates all team-centric features into one page

**Status:** Functions correctly as separate pages but roadmap says merge them. Moderate refactor needed.

---

### FEATURE 5: AGENCY HUB ✅ **STRUCTURE EXISTS, ALL FEATURES COMING SOON**

**File:** `/src/pages/AgencyHub.tsx`

**WHAT EXISTS:**
- ✅ **5 tab structure** (Client Management, CV Reformatter, Placements, Invoicing, Commission)
- ✅ **Tab navigation** with icons
- ✅ **Coming Soon UI** — each tab shows feature description + checklist + "Request Early Access" button
- ✅ **Professional copy** describing each feature
- ✅ **Placeholders ready** for implementation

**CURRENT STATE:**
All 5 tabs are **Coming Soon placeholders**. No functional features yet.

**Tabs:**
1. **Client Management** — Manage hiring clients, mandates, SLAs, comms log
2. **CV Reformatter** — Batch reformat CVs, apply agency branding
3. **Placements** — Track offer → start date, counter-offer risk, guarantee periods
4. **Invoicing** — Auto-generate placement invoices, fee structures, payment tracking
5. **Commission** — Tiered commission calculations, consultant payouts

**Status:** Skeleton is ready. All features deferred (Coming Soon). This is a placeholder for Phase 2+.

---

### SIDEBAR STRUCTURE ❌ **NEEDS REORDERING**

**File:** `/src/components/JobSidebar.tsx` (lines 88-107)

**CURRENT ORDER:**
```
Workspace:
  - Dashboard
  - My Jobs
  - Talent Pool

Tools:
  - Tasks
  - Activity
  - Reports

Organization:
  - Team
  - Agency (→ /agency, currently → /agency-hub per AgencyHub.tsx)
  - Career Page
  - Integrations
  - Billing
  - Settings

Support:
  - Feature Request
  - Changelog
```

**ROADMAP RECOMMENDS:**
```
- Dashboard
- Jobs (My Jobs)
- Candidates (should map to Talent Pool)
- Tasks
- [Agency Hub / Reports?]
- Reports
```

**ISSUES:**
- ❌ **Sidebar says "Agency"** but routes to `/agency` (doesn't match AgencyHub at `/agency-hub`)
- ❌ **Order doesn't match roadmap** — roadmap suggests: Dashboard, Jobs, Candidates, Tasks, Agency Hub, Reports
- ❌ **Current sidebar has extra items** (Career Page, Integrations, Billing, Settings) mixed in Organization section
- ✅ Core items (Dashboard, Tasks, Activity, Team) are all present

**NEEDS WORK:**
- Reorder to match roadmap: Dashboard > Jobs > Candidates (Talent Pool) > Tasks > Agency Hub > Reports
- Fix route mismatch: "Agency" should route to `/agency-hub` (not `/agency`)
- Consider collapsing org/support into dropdown or separate section

**Status:** Navigation items exist but sidebar structure doesn't match recommended order.

---

## SUMMARY TABLE

| Feature | Status | What Works | What Needs Work |
|---------|--------|-----------|-----------------|
| **Tasks** | 90% | Create, assign, status flow, collaboration, real-time | Multi-assign, task comments, change audit |
| **Talent Pool** | 95% | Add, tag, search, assign job, notes, scores | Bulk operations, export |
| **Activity** | 85% | Timeline, filters, real-time, audit log | Email/push alerts, permission filtering |
| **Team Hub** | 60% | Overview + Members + Settings tabs exist | Activity should be 4th tab (currently separate page) |
| **Agency Hub** | 10% | Structure + 5 tabs ready | All features are Coming Soon placeholders |
| **Sidebar** | 70% | All core items present | Order wrong, route mismatch ("Agency" → `/agency` vs `/agency-hub`) |

---

## QUICK WINS (High-Impact, Lower Effort)

1. **Merge Activity into Team Hub** — Move Activity.tsx logic into Team.tsx as 4th tab
2. **Fix sidebar route** — Change "Agency" link from `/agency` to `/agency-hub`
3. **Reorder sidebar** — Dashboard > Jobs > Candidates > Tasks > Agency Hub > Reports
4. **Add multi-assign to Tasks** — Create task_assignees junction table for many-to-many

---

## PHASE 2 FEATURES (Deferred but Planned)

- Agency Hub (all 5 modules) — Currently 100% Coming Soon
- Task comments/threads
- Email/push activity notifications
- Bulk candidate operations (archive, tag, export)
- Task change audit trail
